chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskān, from Sulayman ibn Khālid, who said:

I asked him about prayer on a ship. He said: 'He prays standing, and if he cannot stand, he should sit and pray while facing the Qiblah. If the ship turns, he should turn with the Qiblah if he is able to do so; and if he is not able to do so, he should remain in his place and strive to determine the Qiblah.' And he said: 'He prays the voluntary prayer facing the front of the ship, and he is facing the Qiblah when he says the Takbir, then it does not harm him wherever the ship turns.'
ai.seo_question: How should one pray on a ship if it is moving or turning?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the fiqh of *salat al-musafir* (traveler's prayer) on a vessel, establishing a pragmatic hierarchy of postures and orientation that balances ritual precision with the physical realities of maritime travel. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ijtihad* in applying general principles of facing the Qiblah to dynamic environments, ensuring the validity of both obligatory and voluntary prayers despite the ship's rotation. The ruling underscores the principle of *ease* (*yusr*) in worship, allowing the worshipper to fix their direction at the moment of the opening Takbir for nafl prayers, thereby removing anxiety over continuous orientation.
